ACCESSING AUTISM SERVICES?
We’ve Got You Covered!

DISCLAIMER: Please note that we are not medical professionals, nor is any of our advice official medical advice. This is simply a summary of what we found to be the most helpful on our own individual journeys. No matter what you read online, always verify with recommendations from certified medical professionals!
Learn About...
SERVICE PROVIDERS

There is a wide variety of service providers available, and while some specialize exclusively in Autism support, others offer services that can benefit a broader range of needs. The main types of providers you might encounter include, but are not limited to:
BCBA (Board Certified Behaviour Analyst)

BCBAs, or Board Certified Behaviour Analysts, are highly educated professionals with a graduate level certification in behavior analysis. Professionals certified at the BCBA level are independent practitioners who provide behavior-analytic services (Behavior Analyst Certification Board, 2017). In short, BCBAs focus on behavioural therapy. This means they focus on *changing, improving, and understanding behaviours.
*Particularly on that note, and especially regarding the offering of ABA (Applied Behaviour Analysis) Therapy, it should be noted that there is a controversy around the focus on “changing and improving behaviours”, and that BCBAs are now trying to add an importance of ethical, person-centered practices instead (read more about this in the ‘Study Up!’ section at the bottom of this page).
Thus, it's important to note - not just for BCBAs and/or ABA offeings, but for all service providers - that you should pay attention to styles that best work for you!
OT (Occupational Therapist)

OTs, or Occupational Therapists, are highly educated professionals who aim to people participate in meaningful daily activities, or “occupations,” by addressing their unique mental, physical, emotional, and developmental needs(Finlan, 2014).
Their goal is to empower and foster independence in a way that respects the patient's individual experiences and identities.
SLP (Speech Language Pathologist)

(This is the same as a ST, or Speech Therapist - just a different name) SLPs, or Speech Language Pathologists, are highly educated professionals who support numerous types of speech and swallowing needs. This can include speech delays, differences in fluency of speech, lisps, stutters, swallowing differences, and feeding differences. (About S-LPs, Aud and CHA, n.d.). In other words,SLPs work collaboratively with individuals and their families to develop communication and/or swallowing strategies tailored to their preferences and strengths.
Non Autism-Specific Professionals

There are also other service providers who don't specifically serve children on the autism spectrum, but have services for them. This includes: Early Interventionists, Infant Toddler Development Specialists, Early Childhood Special Education Professionals, Educational Therapists, and Pediatricians, among others. In addition to Autism-specific professionals, there are other service providers who play a key role in supporting the developmental and educational needs of children, including Autistic children. These providers bring valuable expertise to help create inclusive and supportive environments. They include:
- Early Interventionists: Specialists who work with young children to support early developmental milestones.
- Infant Toddler Development Specialists: Professionals focused on the growth and learning of infants and toddlers.
- Early Childhood Special Education Professionals: Educators who design inclusive learning environments tailored to diverse developmental needs.
- Child Development Specialists: Experts in understanding and fostering healthy development in young children.
- Educational Therapists: Providers who use specialized techniques to address learning challenges.
- Pediatricians: Physicians who provide holistic care and guidance for children's physical and developmental health.
Check the bottom of the page for more resources on each of these!
Learn About...
AUTISM SERVICES

A wide range of services is designed to support the unique needs and strengths of Autistic individuals, their families, and their caregivers. These services fall into several key categories outlined below (in alphabetical order, to ensure clarity and accessibility):
Behavioural

Behavioural therapy services are focused on *changing, understanding, and improving behaviours. They are one of the most evidence-backed and proven therapy services, and the most widely known branches of that is ABA (Applied Behaviour Analysis) and IBI (Intensive Behavioural Intervention) *(encourages and discourages certain behaviours to improve overall behaviour). While similar, IBI, like the name, is much more intensive (20-40 hours per week vs 4 or less hours per week, 2-3 year period vs 2-6 month period), is delivered by a professional (vs ABA which can be delivered by anyone), and is largely ineffective after the age of 5 (TVO Today | Current Affairs Journalism, Documentaries and Podcasts, n.d.).
*And like mentioned in the ‘BCBA’ section, it should be noted that with ABA Therapy & related therapy style, there is a controversy around the focus on both “changing and improving behaviours” and “encouraging and discouraging behaviours”, and that BCBAs are now trying to add an importance of ethical, person-centered practices instead. (read more about this in the ‘Study Up!’ section at the bottom of this page).
Thus, it's important to note - not just for BCBAs and/or ABA offeings, but for all service providers - that you should pay attention to styles that best work for you!
Developmental

Developmental therapy services are focused on improving developmetal skills, such as motor skills, speech and language skills, cognitive and intellectual skills, and social and emotional skills (CDC, 2024). Under this category of services, the most widely known branches are SLT (Speech Language Therapy) (working on speech and communication skills), OT (Occupational Therapy) (working on the doing of everyday activities, or occupations), and PT (Play Therapy) (therapy using the therapeutic benefits of play to unlock the development of a person) (Association for Play Therapy, 2015). Sensory therapy (improving reactions to overly sensitive stimuli such as light, sounds, and touch) is also included in this category. (CDC, 2024)
Educational

Educational therapy services are focused on giving school-based treatments. In a classroom-like setting, teachers can focus on a child's learning differences, understand their patterns, and help the child to develop the skills that are missing or underdeveloped. There exist many educational therapists, among others, with a wide range of specialized services for your child. (CDC, 2024) For example, educational therapy can be done in a private setting or a home environment, tailored to individual needs.
Nutritional

Nutritional therapy services are focused on building healthier diets for people with unique dietary preferences. Many (but not all) autistic individuals are sensitive towards certain foods, and that more narrow diet can lead to inadequate nutrition for development (Nutritional Therapy for Autism, 2017). Finding a nutrition specialist (registered dietricians) to create diets that satisfy both nutrition and sensitivity towards certain foods can be crucial for the needs of any individual.
Pharmacological

Pharmacological therapy services are a bit different from the rest. Because, autism is not a condition to be cured, and rather a neurodivergent way of being, pharmacological therapy instead focuses on medications for associated conditions. For both minor and major co-occuring conditions, from sore throats and mild stomach issues, to anxiety and depression, prescribed can be an important part of a holistic support plan, working alongside other therapies and strategies to enhance well-being and quality of life. (CDC, 2024)
Psychological

Psychological therapy services are focused more on working with mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, as well as building self-esteem, emotional regulation, and coping strategies, empowering individuals to navigate challenges. Under this category of services, the most widely known branch is CBT (Cognitive Behaviour Therapy) (helps you or your child recognize patterns between negative-toned thoughts, behaviours, and feelings, along with more positive-toned ones). (CDC, 2024)
Social-Relational

Social-relational therapy services are focused on building social skills and relationship-building skills. They work to help in understanding different perspectives, emotions and feelings. Under this category of services, the most widely known branch is RDI (Relationship Development Intervention) (a combination of everything mentioned before, but also motivating your child to socialize and build relationships). (CDC, 2024)
On this theme, please note that Autistic individuals may have different but equally valid ways of forming relationships and communicating. This highlights the importance of respecting and embracing neurodiverse approaches to social and relational connections, and on focusing on customizing social-relational therapies to align with the individual’s unique needs and social preferences.
Other

Many different service categories and unique therapies can support your loved one’s growth and well-being. Options like animal-assisted therapy, art therapy, and relaxation therapy (CDC, 2024) can offer meaningful benefits by catering to individual interests and needs.
Explore these options, gather information, and consult with professionals to find what best aligns with your preferences. Your observations and insights will help healthcare providers recommend the ideal therapies for each autistic individual’s unique needs.

As always, it's vital to remember that you know your family member best. Make sure to do your research, book the necessary appointments, and pay attention to your child as much as possible, because your doctor can only recommend therapy based on what you know.
